title: Copywriting 101 Checklist

lessons.title: Course Material: Copywriting-101-Checklist.pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Copywriting 101 for Small Businesses – Cheat Sheet  Introduction ü Copy is a direct conversation with the consumer." – Shirley Polykoff ü Copywriting is essential for communicating the value of your company's offering to its potential customers ü Good writing can make a significant difference in your sales and online conversions ü Bad writing can sabotage your marketing efforts  What You Will Learn in This Course ü Copywriting techniques and time-tested formulas ü You can use these skills in any area of your business where you need words to persuade people to take action ü Grab your reader's attention and maintain it throughout your copy ü Basic SEO tips to help you write in such a way that search engines will help visitors find your content ü Tweaks you can make to the formulas you use that will give your copy greater impact and increase conversions  Learning Objectives:  ü Clearly define copywriting and identify ways you can use it in all areas of your marketing to help your business grow.

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  ü Use several copywriting techniques right away that will improve the results of your current sales or marketing copy. ü Take one sales letter, web page, or other piece of marketing content and apply the AIDA formula to create copy that converts and urges your reader to take action. ü Pick 2 SEO techniques that you can use to help your web copy get found and indexed by Google and apply them to your website, sales page or online product page immediately. ü Identify the techniques and strategies used by companies that excel at copywriting and brainstorm ways you can use these tips in your own copy. ü Create an action plan for updating existing copy and improving it using the copywriting techniques you have learned    Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Module 1 - What Is Copywriting?  ü The process of writing advertising or promotional copy.  ü Explains your product or service ü Copywriting is used on: o Web pages o Press releases o Blog posts o Articles o eBooks o Sales Pages & Landing Pages … and in many other ways  The Purpose of Copywriting ü The purpose of copywriting is to lead a user to take action ü Opening an email ü Clicking a link and visiting a site ü Connecting with the company on social media ü Communicating with and engaging with the company ü Referring the site or company to others ü Signing up for an email newsletter or email list ü Searching for further information ü Downloading a file or free product ü Making an appointment with the company  ü "Liking" or sharing content on social media ü Watching a video to learn more

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  Why is Copywriting Important?  ü Each word has the potential to impact a person’s thinking ü The first contact with a customer ü Grabs attention and communicates benefits quickly ü Communicate your business’s message   Action Steps: Visit your own website home page, a product/service sales page, or other main piece of marketing material you’ve been using for a while.  Ask yourself: 1. What would my first impression be if I didn’t already know my company or product/service?  2. Is the content up-to-date?  3. Does the copy portray my company in a professional manner?  4. Are there typos or formatting errors on the page?  Jot down some notes about anything else you notice to refer back to later.

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  Module 2 - How to Become a Better Copywriter Today Before You Start Writing ü Copywriters get paid a lot for small amounts of text ü It has to be as effective as possible ü Your copy needs to speak directly to your readers ü You need to know  o Demographics o Psychographics o Purchase History o Emotions o Language and Tone o Questions o Doubts o Long-Term Goals o SEO o Your unique value proposition o The Goal of Your Copy  Other Things to Consider ü Unique Value Proposition (UVP) ü Goal of Your Copy

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  Tips on Writing Great Copy That You Can Use Today ü Check grammar, spelling & punctuation ü Always work on sharpening your writing skills ü Write conversationally  Writing Headlines and Subject Lines ü Spend half your time writing & refining your headline ü Focus on grabbing the reader’s attention ü Keep your headlines brief ü Implement the Four U’s o Unique o Ultra-Specific o Urgent o Useful  Pique curiosity with your headline ü Ask Questions ü “How To” ü Identify the reader ü Negative Superlatives ü Deliver on the promise of the headline

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  The "Magic Words" of Copywriting ü Learn the words that resonate with your audience ü Look at successful copy in your niche ü Conduct split-testing  Copywriting Formatting ü Put the most important info at the top ü Break up text with headers and sub-headers ü Use short paragraphs ü List with bullet points ü Go easy on bold and italics ü No underlining ü Think about capitalization ü Use clear fonts that don’t distract ü Keep it simple ü Strip it down ü Use pictures ü Emphasize the call to action  Adding Social Proof to Your Copy ü Testimonials ü Endorsements ü Awards and Certifications ü Customer reviews ü Social media proof

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  ü Customer-generated content ü Install a counter ü Keep all social proof genuine  Testing Your Copy ü Split-testing ü Site analytics ü Direct feedback from visitors ü Peer review  Cleaning Up Your Copy ü Remove anything that can be taken the wrong way ü Change passive to active voice ü Read your copy aloud ü Give it the ‘so what?’  ü Eliminate adjectives and adverbs ü Use as many action verbs as possible ü Don’t use words that describe uncertainty ü Cut out jargon ü Watch out for hyperbole ü Cut anything that doesn’t help you reach your objective

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  Action Steps: 1. Pick at least 1 current piece of your content which you’ll use to apply the copywriting tips you learned in this module. 2. Pick two or three tips or guidelines discussed in the module to focus on applying what you’ve just learned to your current copy.  3. Write down in your notes what changes you will make to your current copy, based on the tips you selected and how you will improve your website copy using these techniques for writing better copy.

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  Module 3 - 8 Proven Copywriting Formulas  ü Formulas are created to make it easier to write copy ü Learn several proven formulas copywriters use  AIDA – Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action Attention ü Grab the reader’s attention with an irresistible headline Interest ü Keep their interest by keeping it relevant Desire ü Stimulate desire using your knowledge of what they want Action ü Give them a call-to-action to take the next step  Before-After-Bridge Before ü What life is like now. Identify the problem faced After ü Get them to imagine a wonderful future where this problem no longer exists Bridge ü Explain how to get from the Before to the After

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11  Problem-Agitate-Solve Problem ü Identify the readers problem Agitate ü Make them feel the pain by agitating it Solve ü Offer the solution, gained through the action you want the reader to take  Features-Advantages-Benefits Features ü Describe the unique features of the product or service Advantages ü Explain why these features are outstanding Benefits ü Identify how this makes life better for the reader  5 Basic Objections ü Address the doubts and questions in the buyer’s mind o "I don't have enough time." o "I don't have enough money." o "It won't work for me." o "I don't believe it." o "I don't need it."

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12  The Story Arc The Opening ü Introduce the character and their normal life and explain how an unexpected event changed it The Conflict ü The hero struggles with their pain and the trouble it has cause them The Solution ü The protagonist discovers a solution to makes things normal again and they’re offering it to you  Picture-Promise-Prove-Push Picture ü Paint a picture of the type of life your reader is dreaming of Promise ü Describe how your product or service will deliver them to this life Prove ü Back up your claims with proof Push ü Ask for a commitment and tell them what they need to do  The 3 Reasons Why ü Three questions in the readers’ mind o Why are you the best? o Why should I believe you? o Why should I buy (take action) right now?

PAGE_13:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 13  Action Steps: These are just a few formulas to get you started. There are many more you can test out. Try different formulas and you will find that there are certain formulas that are especially effective with your target market. 1. Pick one of your major products or services that you sell to customers. 2. Using the AIDA technique, create an outline for a sales letter or marketing piece that addresses each part of the formula. 3. Choose another of the above formulas and try writing copy for a product or service of yours.  Don’t worry about filling in all the text of the content. Just focus on addressing the 4 parts of the AIDA formula or another formula you’ve chosen.

PAGE_14:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 14  Module 4 - How to Get Your Content Found: SEO Tips   ü Copy won't benefit your business if it can't be found  ü SEO is important to keep in mind   How Search Engines Find Website Content ü There are a set of algorithms that search engines use to rank and find content ü Google crawls websites and collects data about them  What This Means for Your Web Copy ü You can increase the likelihood that your website will be found by the search engine by using key words and phrases ü Use
